critique.evidence: Desktop has a strong cyber-lab identity, disciplined dark palette, bold headline, and clear cyan/red accents. However, responsive polish falls short: tablet and mobile atlas columns begin visibly clipped, labels are truncated, and the grid leaves large dead vertical areas. The mobile detail panel and JSON block feel excessively long and cramped. Headers are also visually crowded: desktop shows overlapping/faint navigation text, tablet truncates the brand and nav, and mobile provides little location context. Several tiny, low-contrast mono labels weaken legibility.
critique.fix: Recompose the atlas for narrow screens as a deliberate paged or snap-scrolling stage carousel with complete column headers and visible position state; remove clipped partial columns and collapse unused grid height. Tighten the detail/JSON presentation, raise small-text contrast and size, and replace the crowded responsive header with a clean compact navigation pattern.
